posts.author: Andy Dean
posts.content_md:
After reading page after page of “criticism” thought I would start a thread on a positive note.

For me the one hologram that stands out is “The Painter,” by John Perry Please see links below.

I first sew this hologram in the Chicago Museum of holography, and was blown away by it.

It was not the biggest or technically advanced hologram I had ever seen but it was the most “complete” hologram I have ever seen. It’s a hologram about holography. 

I always liked the Quote “Holography is painting with light” and as I turned and stud at the far end of the dark gallery space, there at the far end was the aprox 4 feet by 4feet Transmission hologram. I saw the bearded figure holding a paint brush through a “goldish” picture frame and the quote came flooding back. For some reason I began to walk across and towards the hologram and was amazed to see the figure swish the paint brush through the air leaving a trail of paint which changed colour as I moved.

It is the holograms content and its interacted with me as I moved that still to this day makes it the best hologram I have ever seen.

Andy. 

![Image](http://www.holonorth.com/lgpainter.jpg)

[http://www.holonorth.com/stock.htm](http://www.holonorth.com/stock.htm)

You will find an amimation and more info here.

My favorite hologram years ago was in a gallery in Wash. D.C. It was of a microscope that was image planed where you could walk up to the eyepiece that was sticking out of the hologram by a coulple of inches and look into the eyepiece. You could only see what was in the microscope and not the rest of the hologram. I was like looking in an actuall microscope. That was great.

Now the best holograms I like are from Lasart. August has some of the brightest and intersting hologram I have ever seen. I especially like his Solid Air collection. They are amazing to see in person.

[http://www.lasart.com/solidair/index.html](http://www.lasart.com/solidair/index.html)

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md:
[quote:0d1ff73ab7]It's description says "Animated, Full-color Transmission". What does that mean? What would be the lighting requirements?[/quote:0d1ff73ab7]

It's probably a stereogram or a multiple channel, depending whether the movement is smooth or jerky. I suppose a stereogram is just a multiple channel with lotrs of channels. The "Full-color" probably means that it's a so-called "pseudo-color" rainbow., where you superimpose slits so that at the right viewpoint you see full color. I was going to talk about this at PCGII if it happens.

Best hologram I ever saw would be the Dizzy Gillespie. I felt I had to actually duck under the extended trumpet, or whatever the musical instrument was.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Andy, I bet that is excellent in real life. Let me ask a question, Obviously the hologram is larger then the "picture frame" right? This allows the illusion that the paint is extending beyond the frame as represented in the animation. If this is the case, which I believe it is, then this has to be one of the best, most thought out hologams ever. This is a step in the direction of the Princess Lea hologram, if only an illusion that it is a step in that direction. How far in front of the actual plate is the paint trail?

What a difficult question. There are so many good holograms and I have a hard time judging which one I've seen is the "best".

How about my favorite?

That's got to be the one that really got me started which is the cube hologram that came with the Holography Handbook back in the '80s. I spent hours outside staring at it while stockpiling the material I'd need to build my own lab.

I like holograms which are less 'wow' and more emotion. Faces tend to be the most stirring for most people, including myself. I first saw this on eBay and then found numerous references to it, although not many decent pictures.

Here's an OK photo of it (link lifted from a great gallery <a href=[http://www.guillermito2.net/holo/>here</a](http://www.guillermito2.net/holo/%3Ehere%3C/a)>).

![Image](http://www.guillermito2.net/holo/gurltree1.jpg)

BTW-MichaelH, I know exactly which 'cube' you are refurring to. I happen to have the Holography Handbook laid out on a counter here and glanced at it again after you mentioned it. I thought about doing a Denisyuk of something similar, but of pieces of white tagboard which formed a grid of cubes (hard to describe) and which had a poem or something written not just down, but across, so you had to read 'around' the surfaces to get the whole thing.

-Phil
